# Overview {#sec-overview}

This pipeline asks a two-part question in skeletal-muscle proteomes of cancer
survivors:

1. **What does cancer recovery do to the muscle proteome?** — the *disease axis*
   (cancer-recovery baseline vs healthy controls).
2. **Does exercise training move that proteome back toward healthy?** — the
   *training axis*, and a formal **rejuvenation / signature-reversal** analysis.

The design is deliberately reduced to **three groups** so each contrast answers
one clean question, and the supplement (creatine vs placebo) is pooled out
because it is not the question of interest here.

| `group_time` | Meaning | n samples |
|---|---|---|
| `H_pre`   | Healthy controls, single timepoint | 10 |
| `CR_pre`  | Cancer-recovery subjects, pre-training (CRE+PLA pooled) | 15 |
| `CR_post` | Cancer-recovery subjects, post-training (CRE+PLA pooled) | 14 |

The three contrasts built on this scheme:

| Contrast | Definition | Question |
|---|---|---|
| **`CRvH_Baseline`** (D) | `CR_pre − H_pre`   | Disease deviation from healthy |
| **`CR_Training`** (T)   | `CR_post − CR_pre` | Effect of training |
| **`Resid`** (R)         | `CR_post − H_pre`  | What remains after training (R = D + T) |

Architecture (shared house style): each stage is a numbered folder with
`a_script/` (code), `b_reports/` (proteoDA QC PDFs + figures), `c_data/`
(RDS hand-offs + one consolidated `.xlsx`). Stages are **self-cleaning**: a
re-run wipes its own outputs first, so stale artifacts never accumulate.

```
00_input/        raw matrix, metadata, HPA reference
01_Filtering/    contaminant + missingness + outlier filtering  → DAList_filtered.rds
02_Normalization/ cycloess + (imp4p | mscoreutils) imputation   → DAList_normalized.rds
03_DEP/
  a_non_imputed/  PRIMARY limma DE (NA-tolerant)                → combined_results_pi.csv
  b_imputed/      imputed DE (concordance check)
04_Figures/       publication composites
  Reversal/       rejuvenation analysis (φ, fry, RRHO2) + composite
```

# Stage 00 — Inputs {#sec-inputs}

Three files drive everything downstream.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `00_input/CvH_raw.xlsx` | DIA-MS protein matrix, **3,172 protein groups × 46 columns** (5 annotation cols + 41 samples) |
| `00_input/CvH_meta.csv` | Analysis sample sheet (`Col_ID`, `Subject_ID`, `Group`, `Timepoint`, `Group_Time`, `Supplement`), one row per sample |
| `00_input/HPA_annotations.tsv` | Human Protein Atlas reference (12,894 genes): secretome location, blood concentration, single-cell nCPM, protein class |

The sample sheet is taken as given; from its `Group_Time` column we derive the
pooled 3-group `group_time`, then align the matrix to it by `Col_ID` — a
mismatch errors immediately, which is the only check worth keeping:

```{r}
#| label: load-metadata
metadata <- readr::read_csv(here::here("00_input", "CvH_meta.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
metadata$group_time <- dplyr::case_when(
  metadata$Group_Time %in% c("CRE_T1", "PLA_T1") ~ "CR_pre",
  metadata$Group_Time %in% c("CRE_T2", "PLA_T2") ~ "CR_post",
  metadata$Group_Time == "H_T1"                  ~ "H_pre")
```

# Stage 01 — Filtering {#sec-filtering}

This is the stage the study most cares about getting right: **systematically and
defensibly removing blood-plasma contaminants** from a muscle biopsy proteome,
without throwing away real muscle biology.

## Why blood contamination matters {#sec-blood-why}

Needle biopsies are perfused with blood. Plasma proteins (albumin, hemoglobins,
immunoglobulins, complement, apolipoproteins) are extremely abundant and bury
the muscle signal. But naïvely removing "anything found in blood" also deletes
real muscle proteins that legitimately appear in plasma MS (collagens, VIM, FLNA
in vessel walls). We therefore use a **rule that requires a plasma/blood origin
*and* not a muscle origin**, sourced entirely from the Human Protein Atlas.

## The classifier (inline in Stage 01) {#sec-blood-rule}

A protein is flagged **remove** if it is plasma-origin **and not** muscle-origin:

- **plasma-origin** = HPA Secretome location is *"Secreted to blood"*, **or** it
  is an immunoglobulin gene, **or** its single-cell erythrocyte signal is high
  (`Erythrocytes ≥ 5000 nCPM` — captures the hemoglobins);
- **muscle-origin rescue** = high skeletal-myonuclei single-cell signal
  (`Myonuclei ≥ 50 nCPM`) — a protein with real myofiber expression is kept even
  if it also circulates.

```{r}
#| label: blood-classifier
bl <- readr::read_tsv(here::here("00_input", "HPA_annotations.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::transmute(gene = Gene, uniprot = Uniprot, protein_class = `Protein class`,
    secretome = `Secretome location`,
    ery = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`Single Cell Type RNA - Erythrocytes [nCPM]`)),
    myo = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`Single Cell Type RNA - Myonuclei [nCPM]`))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    secreted_blood = secretome == "Secreted to blood" & !is.na(secretome),
    is_ig          = stringr::str_detect(dplyr::coalesce(protein_class, ""), "Immunoglobulin genes"),
    is_erythrocyte = !is.na(ery) & ery >= 5000,
    muscle_keep    = !is.na(myo) & myo >= 50,
    verdict = dplyr::if_else(!muscle_keep & (secreted_blood | is_ig | is_erythrocyte),
                             "remove", "keep"))
remove_genes <- bl$gene[bl$verdict == "remove"]
```

The erythrocyte cut was raised to 5000 nCPM specifically because lower cuts pull
in housekeeping proteins inflated in enucleate cells; the platelet arm was
dropped for the same noise reason. This keeps the removal list dominated by
*bona fide* plasma proteins (hemoglobins, albumin, complement, Ig).

## Full filtering cascade {#sec-filter-cascade}

```{r}
#| label: filter-cascade
dal <- zero_to_missing(DAList(data = int_mat, annotation = annot_df, metadata = meta_df))
# 1. keep only proteins present in the HPA reference (annotation coverage)
# 2. drop blood-contaminant genes (verdict == "remove")
# 3. native missingness filter: >=5 valid values in >=1 group
dal <- filter_proteins_by_group(dal, min_reps = 5, min_groups = 1,
                                grouping_column = "group_time")
```

> **Implementation note.** `proteoDA::filter_proteins_by_annotation()` is broken
> under R ≥ 4.4 (an internal length-2 `class()` check errors), so the
> annotation-based removals are done by direct matrix subsetting. The
> *group/sample* filters stay native (`filter_proteins_by_group`,
> `filter_samples`) — they use `inherits()` and work fine.

**Frozen filtering log:**

| Step | Proteins after | Removed | % of raw |
|---|---|---|---|
| Raw input | 3,172 | — | 100.0 |
| HPA presence | 2,962 | 210 | 93.4 |
| Blood-contaminant removal | 2,816 | **146** | 88.8 |
| Missingness (≥5 in ≥1 group) | **2,555** | 261 | 80.5 |

## Outlier detection {#sec-outliers}

Samples are flagged by a **4-method consensus** (a sample is dropped only if
≥3 of 4 methods agree — robust to any single method's quirk):

1. **Missingness** — high % missing, or a large pre/post jump in a paired subject;
2. **Median-intensity MAD** — global signal level far from the cohort median;
3. **PCA Mahalanobis** — multivariate outlier on PC1–3 (χ² at p<0.01);
4. **Correlation** — low median inter-sample correlation.

```{r}
#| label: outlier-consensus
outlier_diag <- tibble(Col_ID = colnames(dal$data),
                       miss_flag, mad_flag, pca_flag, cor_flag) |>
  mutate(n_flags = miss_flag + mad_flag + pca_flag + cor_flag,
         consensus_outlier = n_flags >= 3)
dal <- filter_samples(dal, !(Col_ID %in% outlier_ids))
```

Two samples were dropped by consensus: **`CR9_T1` and `CR10_T1`**. Final
filtered matrix: **2,555 proteins × 39 samples**, saved as
`01_Filtering/c_data/DAList_filtered.rds`, with a single
`filtering_report.xlsx` and a `b_reports/blood_contaminants.pdf` summary bar chart.
The workbook is written for **manual review** — `contaminants_removed` and
`contaminants_rescued` each carry the protein name, description, and the HPA
evidence (secretome, blood concentration, erythrocyte / myonuclei signals) behind
every keep/remove call, so the blood filter is auditable by eye rather than by a
test harness. Sheets: `filter_log`, `contaminants_removed`, `contaminants_rescued`,
`outlier_diagnostics`, `blood_classification`.

# Stage 02 — Normalization & imputation {#sec-norm}

## Normalization {#sec-norm-cycloess}

Cyclic-loess normalization via proteoDA's native `normalize_data()`, bracketed
by its own QC reports so the choice is auditable (`write_norm_report` compares
methods; `write_qc_report` shows the post-normalization state).

```{r}
#| label: normalize
dal <- readRDS(here::here("01_Filtering", "c_data", "DAList_filtered.rds"))
write_norm_report(dal, grouping_column = "group_time",
                  output_dir = report_dir, filename = "norm_comparison.pdf")
dal <- normalize_data(dal, norm_method = "cycloess")
write_qc_report(dal, color_column = "group_time", output_dir = report_dir,
                filename = "qc_normalized.pdf")
saveRDS(dal, file.path(data_dir, "DAList_normalized.rds"))   # clean hand-off
```

The normalized matrix **keeps its missing values** — this is deliberate. The
primary DE test (§4) is NA-tolerant, so we never impute before testing.

## Imputation (for multivariate methods only) {#sec-imputation}

Imputation is provided as **two independent options** in
`02_Normalization/imputation/a_script/`, used *only* by downstream methods that
require a complete matrix (figures, rotation tests, WGCNA) — never by the
primary DE test.

- **`a_imp4p.R` — canonical.** Mechanism-aware multiple imputation
  (`imp4p::impute.mi`): MCAR positions filled with `mle`, MNAR positions with
  `igcda` (left-censored). This respects that low-abundance proteins are
  missing-not-at-random.
- **`b_mscoreutils.R` — comparison.** `imputeLCMD::model.Selector` partitions
  MAR vs MNAR, then `MsCoreUtils::impute_matrix(method = "mixed")` applies kNN to
  MAR and QRILC to MNAR positions.

```{r}
#| label: imp4p
conds <- factor(dal$metadata$group_time)
imp <- imp4p::impute.mi(tab = as.matrix(dal$data), conditions = conds,
                        methodMCAR = "mle", methodMNAR = "igcda")
saveRDS(dal_imp, here("02_Normalization", "imputation", "c_data", "DAList_imputed_imp4p.rds"))
```

# Stage 03 — Differential expression {#sec-dep}

## Why non-imputed is primary {#sec-dep-primary}

The gold standard for the DE *test* is **not to impute** — `limma` handles
per-protein missing values natively, whereas imputing before testing
artificially shrinks variances and inflates false positives. So:

- **`a_non_imputed/` is PRIMARY** (the matrix with NAs);
- **`b_imputed/` is a concordance check** (imp4p canonical + mscoreutils).

## Model & repeated measures {#sec-dep-model}

```{r}
#| label: dep-model
dal <- add_design(dal, "~ 0 + group_time + (1 | Subject_ID)")
dal <- add_contrasts(dal, contrasts_vector = c(
  "CRvH_Baseline = CR_pre - H_pre",
  "CR_Training   = CR_post - CR_pre",
  "Resid         = CR_post - H_pre"))
dal <- fit_limma_model(dal)
dal <- extract_DA_results(dal, pval_thresh = 0.10, lfc_thresh = 0, adj_method = "BH")
```

The `(1 | Subject_ID)` term is the key to **within-subject** modelling: CR
subjects contribute paired `CR_pre`/`CR_post` samples, healthy controls
contribute one. proteoDA routes this through `limma::duplicateCorrelation`,
estimating **one consensus correlation** (ρ̂ ≈ **0.25**) that accounts for the
repeated measurement, then fits with `eBayes(robust = TRUE)`. Significance uses
the **Π-score** (Xiao 2014, `Π = P.Value^|logFC|`, threshold < 0.05), which
ranks by significance *and* effect size, alongside BH-FDR.

## Frozen results {#sec-dep-results}

| Contrast | n | FDR < 0.10 | Π < 0.05 (↑ / ↓) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CRvH_Baseline** (disease) | 2,555 | **686** | 504 (350 ↑ / 154 ↓) |
| **CR_Training** (training)  | 2,555 | 0 | 55 (27 ↑ / 28 ↓) |
| **Resid** (residual)        | 2,555 | 562 | 477 (337 ↑ / 140 ↓) |

The disease axis is strong (686 FDR hits); the *training* axis has **no FDR
hits** but 55 Π-score hits — training is a subtle, distributed effect, which is
exactly why the set-level reversal analysis (§5) is the right tool rather than
per-protein training hits.

## Imputed concordance {#sec-dep-concordance}

Running the same model on imputed matrices confirms the strong contrasts are
robust and shows where imputation diverges (the weak training axis):

| Method | CRvH_Baseline | CR_Training | Resid |
|---|---|---|---|
| **imp4p** (canonical) | ρ = 0.92 | ρ = 0.77 | ρ = 0.96 |
| mscoreutils | ρ = 0.78 | ρ = 0.70 | ρ = 0.78 |

Strong-contrast logFCs are highly concordant with the non-imputed primary
(Spearman ρ up to 0.96); the weak `CR_Training` axis is where imputation choice
matters most — another reason the primary DE stays non-imputed.

# Reversal / rejuvenation analysis (`04_Figures/Reversal/`) {#sec-reversal}

The headline biological question: **does training reverse the cancer-recovery
proteome back toward healthy?** This analysis is downstream of the primary DEP
(it reads `03_DEP/a_non_imputed/c_data/combined_results_pi.csv`) but lives with
its figure: engine = `04_Figures/Reversal/a_script/reversal.R`, consumed by the
panels via `a_script/reversal_inputs.R`.

## The rejuvenation fraction φ {#sec-phi}

Each protein has a level at three points: **healthy (H)**, **cancer-recovery
before training (CR_pre)**, and **after training (CR_post)**. From the §4 contrasts,
the **disease deviation** is **D = CRvH_Baseline = CR_pre − H** (how far the disease
pushed the protein from healthy) and the **training response** is
**T = CR_Training = CR_post − CR_pre** (how far training moved it). The third
contrast, **`Resid` = CR_post − H = D + T**, is just the gap *still* left after
training — a plain difference, **not** the reversal itself.

The reversal question is separate: *did training move the protein back toward
healthy?* The **rejuvenation fraction** answers it as "what fraction of the disease
change did training undo":

$$\varphi = -\,T / D$$

The disease moved the protein by **D**; undoing it fully means moving back by **−D**,
so φ is training's reversing size over the disease's size:

- **φ = 0** → training did nothing (T = 0); the protein stays at its diseased level;
- **0 < φ < 1** → partial reversal — some of the disease change undone;
- **φ = 1** → exact reversal (T = −D); the protein is back to healthy and
  residual `Resid = D(1 − φ) = 0`;
- **φ > 1** → overshoot past healthy; **φ < 0** → training **amplifies** the disease change.

So `Resid` (the leftover gap, a difference) and φ (the fraction undone, a ratio)
are two views of the same story, tied by **`Resid` = D·(1 − φ)**.

Disease-signature proteins (Π < 0.05 on D) are classified with a ±0.25 band:

| Class | Rule | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **Normalized**  | φ ≥ 0.25  | training reverses ≥25% of the disease deviation |
| **Persistent**  | \|φ\| < 0.25 | disease deviation largely unchanged by training |
| **Exacerbated** | φ ≤ −0.25 | training pushes further from healthy |

```{r}
#| label: phi
wide <- load_reversal_table("03_DEP/a_non_imputed/c_data/combined_results_pi.csv")
phi  <- compute_phi(wide, band = 0.25)   # disease_sig = sig_pi_D != 0
```

## Guarding against shared-baseline circularity {#sec-circularity}

D and T **share the `CR_pre` samples**, so a structural negative correlation
between their fold-change vectors is mathematically guaranteed (Smyth & Altman
2013, the two-channel reference-design result). A naïve "reversal exceeds zero"
claim would be partly an artifact. The engine therefore tests the **right** null:

> **Protein-label permutation null** — does the *disease-DEP set* reverse **more
> than random proteins** under the *same* shared-baseline structure? It reassigns
> DEP membership to random proteins of equal size, holding all fold changes
> fixed, and compares the observed reversal fraction to that background.

```{r}
#| label: perm-null
null <- reversal_permutation_null(phi, n_perm = 2000, seed = 42)
# obs reversal fraction vs background distribution → z, empirical p
```

This is corroborated by two model-aware / non-parametric methods that do not
share the circularity weakness:

- **fry** (ROAST-family rotation, run **within the limma model** with
  `block = Subject_ID` + duplicateCorrelation) — tests whether the disease-Up /
  disease-Down sets move in the *reversing* direction under training. Run on the
  imp4p matrix (rotation tests need a complete matrix). **camera** is the
  competitive complement.
- **RRHO2** — threshold-free rank–rank hypergeometric; the off-diagonal
  quadrants (disease-Up × training-Down, disease-Down × training-Up) are the
  reversal hotspots.

```{r}
#| label: rotation-rrho2
rot  <- reversal_rotation_test(dal_imp, phi)   # fry (block) + camera
rrho <- reversal_rrho2(phi)                    # 4-quadrant concordance map
```

## Frozen reversal results {#sec-reversal-results}

On the **504 disease-signature proteins** (350 ↑ / 154 ↓):

- **70.8 % reverse** with training, and this **exceeds the random background**
  under the circularity null: permutation **p = 0.0005, z = 4.72**. The reversal
  is real, not an artifact of the shared baseline.
- **Directional asymmetry** (a novel proteome-level finding): disease-**down**
  proteins normalize more than disease-**up** ones — **77.3 % vs 68.0 %**
  reversed (two-proportion p = 0.045). Mechanistically consistent with
  constitutive proteins lost to cachexia/disuse being passively restored by
  anabolic signalling, while actively-driven up-regulated programs resist.
- **fry**: disease-Up→Down p = 0.66, disease-Down→Up p = 0.13 (conservative, both
  directionally reversing); **camera** (competitive) p = 5×10⁻⁷ and 4×10⁻⁵.
- Global Spearman(D, T) = −0.32 (all proteins), −0.42 (disease signature) — the
  signature reverses more strongly than the structural background.

These tables (`phi_table`, `class_counts`, asymmetry, `permutation_null`,
`global_correlation`, `fry`, `camera`, RRHO2) are recomputed on the fly within
the reversal figure stage by the engine — there is no separate upstream runner.

# Figures {#sec-figures}

The reversal composite (`04_Figures/Reversal/`) is the analytical centrepiece —
five panels, all driven by the engine outputs via a thin back-compat adapter
(`a_script/reversal_inputs.R`) and a regenerated pathway-NES cache
(`a_script/00_build_fgsea_cache.R`):

- **A** Quadrant-ORA scatter (per-protein landscape, enriched pathways per quadrant)
- **B** Protein-to-pathway sankey
- **C** fry rotation test (running-enrichment curves)
- **D** Pathway-NES scatter (disease vs training, with Spearman + Fisher-Z CI)
- **E** RRHO2 (threshold-free 4-quadrant concordance map)

![CvH reversal composite — `04_Figures/Reversal/b_reports/main/png/MAIN_Reversal_composite.png`](04_Figures/Reversal/b_reports/main/png/MAIN_Reversal_composite.png)

`04_Figures/Reversal/c_data/Reversal_supplementary.xlsx`. The proteome-overview,
baseline, and training figures live in `04_Figures/F01`–`F08`.

# Reproducibility {#sec-repro}

Run the stages in order from the project root; each stage self-cleans and writes
an RDS hand-off the next stage reads:

```bash
Rscript 01_Filtering/a_script/01_run_filtering.R
Rscript 02_Normalization/a_script/01_run_normalization.R
Rscript 02_Normalization/imputation/a_script/a_imp4p.R        # canonical
Rscript 02_Normalization/imputation/a_script/b_mscoreutils.R  # comparison
Rscript 03_DEP/a_non_imputed/a_script/01_run_dep.R            # PRIMARY
Rscript 03_DEP/b_imputed/a_script/01_run_dep_imputed.R        # concordance
Rscript 04_Figures/Reversal/a_script/00_build_fgsea_cache.R   # pathway cache + rejuvenation engine
Rscript 04_Figures/Reversal/a_script/main/90_stitch_main.R    # composite
```

**Key design decisions, in one place:**

- 3-group pooled scheme; supplement effect intentionally removed.
- Repeated measures via `(1 | Subject_ID)` → duplicateCorrelation (single ρ̂).
- Blood filtering = HPA secretome + erythrocyte signals, rescued by myonuclei.
- DE test on the **non-imputed** matrix; imputation (imp4p canonical) only for
  complete-matrix methods.
- Π-score (Xiao 2014 Eq. 2) for significance + effect size.
- Reversal φ = −T/D, validated against a protein-label permutation null for the
  shared-`CR_pre` circularity, with fry + RRHO2 corroboration.
